$comment: Photos used on the site. `src` is relative to the originals folder (not in the repo). `maxWidth` caps the largest generated width. `focus` is the CSS object-position used when the image is cropped. Callout coordinates for HUD overlays live in src/lib/data/hud.ts.

photos.alt: Drone view at sunset of the Ketura solar field: rows of blue panels on pale desert ground beneath the dark Edom mountains, with sun rays breaking through clouds.
Wide aerial view of the Arava valley with the PV field between date-palm plantations and open desert.
Oblique drone view of the PV field surrounded by bare desert, the reference background for the measurements.
Aerial view of the edge of the Yatir pine forest, where planted forest meets the open semi-arid shrubland.
Yatir forest from above: thousands of Aleppo pines planted on the hills at the northern edge of the Negev desert.
Straight-down drone image of the PV field: parallel rows of dark blue panels separated by strips of bright sandy soil.
Straight-down drone image of the Yatir forest: dark green pine crowns and their shadows on brown ground.
The Weizmann Institute's mobile eddy-covariance laboratory, a white four-wheel-drive truck, parked in the desert with its measurement mast in the background.
The mobile measurement mast standing in the bare, stony desert background next to the PV field.
The measurement mast set up between the panel rows of the PV field, with sonic anemometer and radiometers at the top.
Drone view of the mast top above the tilted PV panels.
Close-up of the sensor head on the mast: sonic anemometer, gas analyser inlet, radiometers and temperature probe.
The instrumented mast between PV rows at dusk, seen from a drone.
The permanent eddy-covariance flux tower rising above the Yatir forest canopy.
A researcher working on instruments at the top of the Yatir flux tower above the pine canopy.
Top-down view of the Yatir flux tower among pine crowns.
The PV field at sunrise beneath the mountains of the Arava valley.
Low drone view along the PV panel rows towards Kibbutz Ketura.
Dense green pine canopy of the Yatir forest stretching towards the desert hills.

photos.credit: Adapted from Fig. 1, Stern, Muller et al. 2023, PNAS Nexus 2(11):pgad352 (CC BY 4.0)
photos.alt: Isometric illustration adapted from Fig. 1 of the paper: a desert block with a PV field (D) and its desert background (C), and a pine forest (B) with its desert background (A). Coloured arrows above each surface show reflected sunlight, thermal emission, sensible heat, latent heat and carbon flux; a thermometer marks the cooler forest surface.
